features.statement: Document title is the plain organization name alone, without keyword-stuffed SEO phrasing.
Uses generic language attribute and landmark semantic elements (nav, main, article, figure, figcaption, time) plus descriptive alt text on all images.
Typography uses a Helvetica Neue/Arial system font stack rather than a webfont.
Body text is large (about 17px) with generous, open line height.
Hero h1 is a very large, heavy-weight, left-aligned headline with larger section h2 sizes.
Hero headline is stacked text lines alternating white and orange accent, with no image tiles.
Small letter-spaced uppercase eyebrow labels in teal sit above section headings and subtitles.
Palette is navy, orange accent and pale blue-gray surfaces, with dark navy body text and muted gray-blue secondary text.
Header is a separate white band with icon logo and dropdown nav, topped by a dark navy utility bar.
Uses native form controls such as a select for translation and a contact form, with no SVG icons.
Featured promo appears as a full-width orange strip below the hero with a dark pill CTA.
Hero ends with a full-width diagonal white wedge divider.
Intro content uses two columns: eyebrow, heading and text left, pill-shaped quick-link chips right.
Highlight sections use soft gradient bands with shadowed cards and a clear call-to-action button.
Statistics appear as stacked white cards with orange left border, shadow and dark navy numbers.
Section headings are left-aligned dark text on plain white backgrounds rather than centered over photo bands.
Secondary actions like View All are outlined pill buttons; primary actions are filled pills.
Cards show a small teal date above a smaller bold title.
Dark navy band with white heading and outlined pill tags replaces graphic map content.
Footer is dark navy with a multi-column sitemap of link groups, social links and a newsletter signup.
Link arrows are text characters (→) rather than icon graphics.
Layout uses CSS grid with a constrained, left-aligned container around 1140px.
Markup is lean: a single inline style block, one script, no external stylesheets and few compact hand-written classes.
